newsitem.title: UK: Conoco UK says North Sea MacCulloch start delayed.
newsitem.headline: Conoco UK says North Sea MacCulloch start delayed.

text.p: Conoco UK (Ltd), a unit of DuPont Co's Conoco Inc, said on Thursday the start-up of its MacCulloch field in the central North Sea has been delayed until early next year.
First oil from the field, situated some 250 km north east of Aberdeen, was originally due flow in December 1996.
"MacCulloch is now scheduled to come on stream in early 1997," said a Conoco spokeswoman.
Conoco UK is operator of MacCulloch, in block 15/24b of the UK Continental Shelf, and owns 60 percent.
LASMO Plc owns the other 40 percent.
Conoco said the floating production, storage and offtake vessel (FPSO) Dagmar Maersk was in the final phase of commissioning and outfitting at a Teesside shipyard.
MacCulloch, which was only granted development approval in late November 1995, has estimated recoverable reserves of some 58 million barrels of oil.
Oil output is expected to peak at some 50-60,000 barrels per day (bpd), maintaining that level for 15-18 months.

The crude, similar to North Sea benchmark Brent, will be transported to the Flotta terminal in the Orkney Islands but the FPSO will also be equipped to load shuttle tankers in pipeline capacity is unavailable.
